findings.title: Browser accepted observation fields and magnitudes the native recorder rejected
findings.detail: Unknown fields, spark_load3.5e38, afr_factor1e300 and pressure_factor1e-300 passed the browser guard but failed native parse_observation. Browser collection could therefore advance its cursor for rows the native recorder rejected.
findings.fix: Parent added allowed-key checks, FLT_MAX magnitude checks and F32 positive-pressure qualification, then regenerated the web bundle.
findings.closure_result: The valid observation still accepts; all four reproduced malformed variants reject at both boundaries. Reason mismatch and null evaluated AFR also reject. Root is responsible for the fresh full Chrome cursor-atomicity workflow.

findings.title: Optional-MAP explanation hid an earlier required-input failure
findings.detail: With pure TPS and unavailable MAP, an unconfirmed CLT or capture overflow correctly produced sensors_valid=false and controller fault4, but the binding explanation only said MAP was unavailable and not required. This impaired fault tracing; it did not permit output.
findings.fix: Parent conditioned the optional-MAP explanation on the remaining inputs being valid and supplied explicit ADC/overflow reasons.
findings.closure_result: ASan/UBSan probe now reports the required conversion failure for unconfirmed CLT and Capture overflow latched for overflow. Healthy pure TPS remains valid. Fault flags are unchanged.

findings.title: Accepted noncanonical F32 fixture values formatted differently in browser and native MSL
findings.detail: Both parsers accepted in-range F64 fixtures, but native storage quantized to F32 before formatting. fuel_load45.000002 became native45.0000038 versus browser45.000002, and baro_kpa100.0000045 became100.000008 versus100.000005. Actual native-produced F32 observations were unaffected.
findings.fix: Parent applied Math.fround to load values before the browser MSL numeric formatter and matched AFR negative-factor qualification at F32 precision.
findings.closure_result: Independent rerun now produces equal native/browser numeric rows for the two reproductions, with no differing columns. Null/NaN remain unavailable.
